After a few early offside calls disrupted their rhythm, the visitors finally broke the deadlock in the 22nd minute. Donyell Malen showcased his clinical nature, receiving a pass from Manu Koné and, following an assist by Paulo Dybala , unleashing a powerful strike from outside the box that beat Zion Suzuki . The goal was a just reward for Roma's early dominance, as they controlled 66% of the ball during the opening period. Parma's Resurgence and a Second-Half Turnaround The narrative shifted immediately after the restart. In the 47th minute, Parma stunned the visitors when Hans Nicolussi Caviglia set up Gabriel Strefezza , who finished accurately with his right foot to level the score. The goal ignited the home crowd, and although Strefezza earned a yellow card for his exuberant celebrations, the momentum had firmly swung in Parma's favor. As the game entered its final stages, the tension reached a breaking point. In the 87th minute, it appeared that Parma had secured a famous comeback victory. Nahuel Estévez provided the crucial assist for Mandela Keita , who found the back of the net to put the hosts ahead 2-1. However, the drama was far from over as the match entered an extraordinary period of stoppage time. Stoppage-Time Chaos and the Decisive Penalty In the 94th minute, AS Roma clawed their way back into the game when Devyne Rensch struck a brilliant long-range effort following a pass from Daniele Ghilardi to make it 2-2. The drama intensified in the 99th minute when a VAR check identified a shirt-pull by Sascha Britschgi on Rensch inside the area. The referee awarded a penalty and showed Britschgi a second yellow card, sending him for an early bath. In the 11th minute of added time, Donyell Malen stepped up to the spot. Despite Zion Suzuki getting a hand to the ball, the power of the strike carried it into the net. This final twist ensured AS Roma left the Tardini with all three points, leaving the home side heartbroken after a valiant display.

On May 3, 2026 , the San Siro played host to a pivotal Serie A clash as Inter Milan looked to maintain their momentum against a gritty Parma Calcio 1913 . The atmosphere was electric, with both sets of fans aware that this late-season fixture could prove decisive for their respective league ambitions. Early Pressure and the Breakthrough From the opening whistle, Inter sought to establish dominance through wide play and set-piece situations. Federico Dimarco was particularly active, delivering a succession of dangerous corners in the 2nd, 10th, and 22nd minutes. While the Parma defense held firm during these initial waves of pressure, the home side nearly found the opener in the 7th minute. Marcus Thuram rose highest to meet a cross, directing a powerful header toward goal, but Zion Suzuki was well-positioned to make a comfortable save. Parma struggled to find an attacking rhythm, often seeing their advances halted by the assistant referee's flag, with Enrico Del Prato and Gabriel Strefezza both caught in offside positions during the first half. As the match approached the interval, Inter finally breached the visitors' resistance. In the first minute of stoppage time, Piotr Zielinski turned provider, threading a precise ball through to Marcus Thuram . The French forward made no mistake, clinicaly finishing with his right foot to send the home support into raptures. It was a cruel blow for Parma , who had defended stoutly for the majority of the period only to concede at the very last moment before the break. Reinforcements and the Final Blow The second half saw a more physical contest, punctuated by a yellow card for Piotr Zielinski in the 64th minute for a mistimed challenge. Sensing the need for fresh energy to put the game to bed, the Inter coaching staff opted for a double substitution shortly after, introducing Henrikh Mkhitaryan and Lautaro Martinez for Zielinski and Thuram . The tactical shift paid dividends almost immediately. In the 80th minute, the two substitutes combined beautifully; Lautaro Martinez provided a selfless assist to Henrikh Mkhitaryan , who was left with an easy left-footed tap-in to double the lead. Parma refused to surrender, making several attacking changes of their own, including the introduction of Pontus Almqvist and Nesta Elphege . They nearly clawed their way back into the game in the 89th minute when Hans Nicolussi Caviglia swung a corner into the box, but Elphege ’s header drifted agonizingly wide of the post. It was the closest the visitors would come to challenging the scoreline as Inter ’s defensive discipline remained intact. Defined by Control and Late Drama The closing stages of the match were defined by Inter 's superior game management and ball retention, maintaining 59% possession to starve Parma of any late opportunities. Despite the two-goal cushion, the hosts continued to push for more. In the final minute of regulation time, Davide Frattesi —who had replaced Nicolo Barella —hit a fierce volley on target, but Zion Suzuki produced another fine save to keep the margin at two. Even deep into injury time, the intensity remained high. Franco Carboni was penalized for a trip on Denzel Dumfries , and Alessandro Circati was forced into a desperate clearance to prevent a third goal. When the final whistle eventually sounded after four minutes of added time, Inter celebrated a deserved victory built on a foundation of clinical finishing and tactical depth. For Parma , it was a night of missed half-chances and frustration, as they were unable to convert their 41% possession into meaningful threats against a disciplined Milanese outfit.
